newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland concerned at Paris egg attack on president.
newsitem.headline: Poland concerned at Paris egg attack on president.

text.p: Poland may formally express its concern to France after rightist protesters got close enough to President Aleksander Kwasniewski to hurl eggs at him during a visit to Paris, his spokesman said on Monday.

"The Polish side is considering a diplomatic note to the French government because the event constituted a threat to the life and safety of President Aleksander Kwasniewski," spokesman Antoni Styrczula, voicing concern over French security arrangements, told private Radio Zet from Paris.

The president, a former communist turned social democrat, was entering a theatre to attend a concert during a working visit to the French capital on Sunday when four Polish rightists got close enough to hurl the eggs.
They missed Kwasniewski, but the radio said two members of his party were hit and were planning civil lawsuits against their attackers, who were detained by police.
Kwasniewski began his two-day visit on Sunday in order to attend a Polish festival in Paris promoting the country's bid to join the European Union and NATO, as well as business ties.
He was due on Monday to meet President Jacques Chirac and French business leaders.

The president is frequently heckled during public appearances in Poland by radical rightists, notably the small opposition Republican League, who say his past as a communist government minister before 1989 should disqualify him for the office to which he was elected in 1995.
